question: In 2023, airports under Italy’s national airport plan (NAP) recorded almost 200 million passenger movements and 1 601 059 aircraft movements. No prior planning has ever been conducted for airport infrastructure in Italy, and the expansion of grass airfields has taken place without these being subject to any regulated development planning. In the light of the above: 1.

Given the differences found at NAP airports in respect of Regulation (EU) No 139/2014, how will the Commission see to it that the safety assessment procedures adopted are completely transparent while simultaneously ensuring that aviation regulations are upheld and that airport operations are safe?

What initiatives might the Commission take to ensure that all NAP airport external emergency plans are completely transparent and, given the importance of these plans for safety and emergency management, how could the surrounding communities be involved in drawing them up and reviewing them?

What action can the Commission take to ensure that restriction maps for ICAO obstacle limitation areas are disclosed in full for each NAP airport and to help address any potential shortcomings and operational limitations emerging from airport regulatory plans and the increase in flight volumes, while balancing aviation objectives with due consideration for safety and the local community?
answer: Regulation (EU) 139/2014( (1)) establishes rules aimed at maintaining a high unform level of safety at airports within the scope of the regulation (EU) 2018/1139( (2))( (3)). These airports must obtain a certificate issued by the national competent Authority attesting that the airport infrastructure and procedures are compliant with applicable EU rules.

Such compliance is subject to the national competent Authority oversight, and any change to characteristics of the airport or to its operational procedures must be notified to and approved by the same Authority.

Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 requires Member States to ensure that an emergency plan is established for aviation emergency situations occurring in the aerodrome, as well as in the immediate aerodrome surroundings. It is the aerodrome operator’s responsibility to establish and implement such an aerodrome emergency plan in coordination with the authorities which are responsible for the National or Local Emergency Plan.

EU rules in the field of aerodrome safety include specific provisions addressing protection of aerodrome surroundings. It is the Member States’ responsibility, through its competent Authority, to ensure that consultations are conducted with regard to safety impacts of constructions to be built within and beyond the limits of the obstacle limitation and protection surfaces.
It is the responsibility and prerogative of the Member State to define and implement appropriate coordination and consultation mechanisms.

Commission Regulation (EU) No 139/2014 of 12 February 2014 laying down requirements and administrative procedures related to aerodromes pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 216/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council, OJ L 44, 14.2.2014, p. 1-34.
